text: We as a service provider, a bare metal provider, we set up our servers inside cages, inside tier 3 data centers so they are fully monitored 24 7. text: Yeah, DDoS is super challenging. We saw this recently with the metal ads. Mint. Right. They were heavily attacked and they are using Cloudflare, which is super competent to fight DDoS. But even then, when the attacks are sophisticated enough or they have a lot of throughput, they can take down any kind of application. So DDoS is about two things mainly. One is true, you have to have throughput to ingest those attacks. And the second thing, you need intelligence to mitigate those attacks when they are targeting the application. So for, for throughput, a best practice practice is the provider has a lot of big ports everywhere, distributed across the globe, and you have multiple terabytes of traffic that you can ingest at the edge and do not transport these attacks through the network close to the target. So this is a strategy that any DDoS provider takes. They deploy big ports at the edge and the second thing is distributing DDoS appliances in many places too. So you can mitigate sophisticated layer 7 attacks that are the. That are usually they don't carry a lot of bandwidth, but they use.
